name: involute-gear
why: A module 2, 20-tooth, 20 degree spur gear 10 thick, every flank a certified { curve } on the base circle rb = 20 cos 20 = 18.794. Closed-form section: z * (rf^2 * gap / 2 + ra^2 * psiA + rb^2 * tA^3 / 3) with rf = 17.5, ra = 22, tA = sqrt((ra/rb)^2 - 1) = 0.6085, half-tooth angles psiB = pi/40 + inv 20 = 0.09344 at the base and psiA = 0.03159 at the tip, gap = 2pi/20 - 2 psiB: 1226.106 mm2, so 12261.057 mm3; the mesh reads 0.04 % under it at 0.01 mm, as every curved wall here does. It meshes in 1996 triangles: before vendor patch 0003 the mesher read the involute's slow start on the base circle as deflection and took 20300 (docs/GOTCHAS.md, "A curve that starts slowly meshed in ten times the triangles"). The points are the analytic involute itself: tooth 0's rising flank at roll t = 0.15, 0.35, 0.55, each on the boundary and 0.01 mm either side of it along the involute's normal (sin b, -cos b), b = t - psiB, and tooth 7's falling flank at t = 0.3 and 0.01 mm outside it - so the built flank is held to the equation, not to any points the script drew it through. curve_bound_mm is the bound the script proved from |r''''| = rb sqrt(9 + t^2): eight pieces of tA/8 per flank, sqrt2 * rb * sqrt(9 + tA^2) * h^4 / 384; deviation_mm is the kernel's own reading against points of the involute between the pieces' ends.
